description: A hardy three-leaf sprig from the Cloverfield Plains. A staple reagent for brews.
A firm mushroom cap harvested in Mushroom Hollow. Faintly bitter, mildly restorative.
A humming sliver of Old Crystal Mine ore. Used in enchanted gear.
A weightless plume shed by windmites. Prized by fletchers for swift arrows.
Pale scale-dust from a moonmoth wing. Glows faintly under the Moonwell.
A splinter of living bark from a barkling. Tough enough for light shields.
Luminescent powder ground from sporeling caps. A key mana-draught reagent.
A broken glyph-shard left by rune sentinels. Still warm with arcane charge.
Cold grey residue from a vein wraith. Wards off lesser shadows.
A raw lump of ore pried from the mine walls. The smith always wants more.
A glossy thread combed from Moonwell reeds. It holds enchantments without fraying.
A small pearl that gathers moonlit ripples under its surface.
A translucent shard condensed from an echo beneath the Moonwell.
Warm orange glass shed by the crystal shelves above the Hollow Kiln.
Fine heat-holding ash left when a cinder mote gutters out.
A many-colored plate from a prism scarab, tougher than it looks.
A strand of living summit-light that shines without casting a shadow.
A cool sliver of condensed dusk left behind by a Gloam Warden.
A fine strand spun from light that survived the long shadow above Lanternspire.
A black mirror-shard that catches a sunrise no one else can see.
Sea-bright crystal grown where Glasswind spray dries against the coast.
Strong golden fiber that rises from the tide whenever the morning beacon turns true.
Pale residue from a false beacon-light, still warm enough to guide a compass needle.
A warm clover tonic. Restores a modest amount of health.
A double-steeped tonic for deeper wounds.
Glowcap-infused water that rekindles spent focus.
A pocket of dried spore-cap chips. Restores stamina on the move.
A folded clover poultice that draws out spore venom.
Wraith-ash incense that hardens the skin for a short while.
A feather-light brew that quickens the step for a time.
A cool sip of fen water that restores focus with a silver aftertaste.
Deep Moonwell water that restores a large measure of focus.
A pepper-warm draught that restores focus after a long kilnward climb.
Aurora thread steeped in moonwater. Clears the crushing hush of gloom.
Bottled dawn threaded with voidglass. Raises attack for one bright minute.
A hearty camp bowl thickened with sunwake kelp. Restores substantial health.
A sharp mineral draught that hardens the party against the Glasswind for a short time.
A woven token that whisks the bearer home to Hearthvale Town.
A trainee's practice sword. Light, forgiving, and utterly ordinary.
A quick leaf-bladed knife favored by plains scouts.
A wind-strung longbow that looses arrows on a whistling breeze.
A blade grown from mine crystal. It sings when it strikes.
A round shield of layered living bark. Surprisingly springy.
A faceted focus that hums a protective note.
A simple stitched cap. Keeps the sun and the odd twig off.
A dented iron helm from the Old Crystal Mine, lamp bracket and all.
Sturdy roadworn cloth. The first thing every adventurer buys.
A vest woven from mushroom fibers. Light, breathable, oddly warm.
Armor set with mine crystal. Heavy, radiant, and nearly unbreakable.
A dried four-leaf clover on a cord. Luck, they say, favors its bearer.
A silver band set with lunar stone. Glimmers brightest at the Moonwell.
A tiny blue lantern that burns cold and steady beside still water.
Watcher-woven armor that turns fen silk and tide pearls into a quiet ward.
A clear-edged relic tempered in the Moonwell Heart after the waters were calmed.
Orla forged this bright poleblade around a spark from the restored Hollow Kiln.
Layered prism shell and emberglass spread heat across its broad face.
A light glasswright crown that stays cool while sharpening its wearer's focus.
A mantle woven from Moonwell calm, kiln warmth, and the first light above the vale.
Sunshard filaments hold a sliver of morning just above the wearer's brow.
A radiant ward made from the Herald's broken sign, bright at its rim and dark at its heart.
A coast-forged blade whose bright edge always points toward the next morning.
Sunwake cord and saltglass clasps hold fast without weighing down a long patrol.
A saltglass compass rose that steadies its bearer when every reflection looks like a road.
Silver-green cordage that bends with the causeway wind without fraying.
A wave-shaped plate of dark metal, cool even after the tide withdraws.
A bright pearl carrying a harmless but persistent storm charge.
Reliquary glass that catches lightning a heartbeat before it arrives.
A sharp coast tonic that shakes saltwater and storm drag from the limbs.
A sparkling stormreed cordial that puts a clean tailwind behind every step.
A tideiron spear balanced to hold its line against both surf and sudden wind.
A compact shield that splits a heavy impact into harmless blue sparks.
Layered stormreed and coastwarden cloth made for exposed roads above the sea.
A calm circle cut from the heart of the storm, always showing the safest next step.
A translucent cliff flower petal that softens even the sharpest dawn glare.
Pale blue ore formed where cliff lightning cooled inside the stone.
A strong flight feather that hums when turned into an oncoming wind.
A sun-bright gear from the observatory mechanisms, still warm with measured motion.
Fine silver dust collected where the observatory roof once caught a falling star.
A flawless prism cut to divide daylight into paths the old astronomers could read.
A cool sunveil infusion that clears the white afterimage of hostile light.
A luminous draught that lays a gentle veil between the drinker and hostile magic.
Suspended starfall dust burns cold, lending each strike the certainty of descent.
Skyglass heel plates and stormreed grips make narrow ledges feel almost level.
A narrow prism visor that turns blinding radiance into a clean targeting line.
A crescent blade forged to follow the same swift curve as a turning constellation.
Interlocking auric rings rotate across its face to meet a blow at the perfect angle.
Star-threaded robes whose brass meridians shift to chart danger before it arrives.
Its needle points not north, but toward the next decision that can still change the day.
A highland herb whose pale veins brighten when held beside an honest promise.
A thin golden plate cooled in mountain wind until it became lighter than iron.
Prismwing thread that changes color with the memory of its last open sky.
A curved talon worn smooth by years of turning at the edge of the sunrise.
Living black ink that rearranges itself into a precise record of nearby voices.
A metal-thin archive page that grows new script when carried into daylight.
A perfect index crystal that holds many conclusions without insisting on one.
Dawnsage and powdered sunmetal knit the painful fault lines left by a crushing blow.
A brisk aurora infusion that makes the next distant marker feel close at hand.
A measured archive cordial that restores the body to its strongest recent memory.
Aurell weaves every rescued prism thread into a mantle that moves like an open wing.
Maelis tempers its edge on the direct road, where hesitation has nowhere to hide.
Flexible sunmetal plates carry force around the stride instead of through it.
A guarded memory flame reveals which incoming line was written to harm its bearer.
The restored archive crown leaves room for every path that could still be taken.
Two highland vows share one clasp without erasing the road that was left untaken.
Soft canopy moss that repeats the last clear note sung near it.
Thin living bark whose rings hum when held against worked metal.
A bright beetle carapace that keeps a clean, bell-like tone after shedding.
A forked antler whose branching notes settle into harmony when carried together.
A script-veined leaf preserved beneath Crownroot, still carrying an unfinished refrain.
A glassy fungal spore that rings once before dissolving into alchemical vapor.
Golden resin from the sanctum crown, warm with a chorus of recovered voices.
Echo Moss and bright bark restore a silenced voice before the last note fades.
A cool green tonic that returns spent magic in a rising sequence of clear notes.
Golden resin and hymn leaf restore the body with the steadiness of a held chord.
Layered bark and chime shell turn each impact into useful momentum.
Its resonant limbs make every arrow the final note of a distant warning.
Living script circles the grain and completes each spell in a different hand.
A faceted ward that answers hostile magic with a soft cancelling tone.
Rootsilk vestments bearing every voice once struck from the sanctum record.
Six interlocking lines leave one open space for the technique its bearer chooses.
A lunar seal borne by the Moonwell Guardian. Opens the way to the Moonwell.
A sealed letter the Elder asked you to carry to Millwick.
A carved token proving Watcher Seren sent you. Show it at the gate.
A calm blue stone marking the restoration of the Moonwell Heart.
The banked inner spark of the Kilnheart Colossus, waiting for a gentler purpose.
The last cold point of the Starved Crown, carrying a spark that no longer hungers.
The Herald's divided seal, proof that the new dawn will be watched from both sides.
The true bearing hidden inside the Drowned Meridian, pointing inland at last.
The quiet center left when the Reliquary storm finally remembers how to rest.
The radiant heart of the Celestial Orrery, now holding a steady image of the true sky.
The Keeper's final catalogue, reopened to a blank page instead of a fixed ending.
The Hierophant's silent command, changed into a seed that can hold many voices without ruling them.
A garden petal whose veins briefly hold any mark traced across them.
Clear memorial glass that bends intent toward the tool carrying it.
Supple hide patterned by a Glyphhare's constantly rearranging marks.
A warm antler tine that stores the strength of every path it illuminates.
Stone dust from an erased inscription, eager to carry a kinder purpose.
Dark ore with a pale center, mined from the oldest seams beneath Namesong.
Archive wax that seals a chosen mark without making it permanent.
A reusable attack mark for weapons and accessories. Binding never consumes it.
A reusable warding mark for offhands and body armor.
A living mark that adds deep reserves to headgear, armor, or accessories.
A quickening script for weapons, headgear, and accessories.
A precise mark that reveals the fault line in an enemy's guard.
A floral garden broth that restores 280 HP to the most wounded ally.
Clear vault water that restores 100 MP to the ally most in need.
A balanced engraving hammer equally suited to shaping wayglass and armor.
Petal-laminate armor made for moving between bright marks without disturbing them.
A pale-centered circlet that remembers names while leaving their futures open.
The Archivore's broken seal, carrying every stolen name without binding any of them.
Silver pollen that settles in lines pointing toward the nearest honest road.
Several translucent mineral layers sharing one impossible reflection.
A tempered promise from the Spire, strong only while its bearer still chooses it.
Warm hide streaked by the brief light of a Waystar Grazer’s passage.
A Scarab plate whose grain rotates toward whichever path was most recently chosen.
A patient glow left behind when a Pathless Wisp finally accepts a direction.
A bright thread that remembers two futures without forcing either one to happen.
A bracing moorland tea that restores Severed allies to their non-health rune bonuses.
A dark, peppery trail stew that restores 320 HP to the most wounded ally.
A balanced mark that draws several small strengths into one chosen piece.
A traveling mark that quickens the bearer while keeping their aim on one bright point.
A long waysteel blade balanced around the next step rather than the last victory.
Layered glass that holds because its bearer keeps choosing whom to protect.
A silver-lined hood that keeps falling lights from becoming distractions.
Weather-dark armor made to cross open moorland without losing a chosen bearing.
A ring with twelve open lines and no inscription claiming which one must be followed.
The Crown’s central stone, opened into twelve paths that now answer instead of command.
